_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::poisson#1 — for a pure Poisson problem VELOCITYFIELD may simply be left out, because 'zero' is already its default. On a stationary TRANSP TRI3 deck the explicit and the omitted arms both exit 0 with the same result test CORRECT at 1e-12; the omitted arm prints no diagnostic at any severity (OMITTED_ERROR_LINES=0) and the substring 'velocit' appears zero times in its whole log (OMITTED_MENTIONS_VELOCITY=0). The control arm is VELOCITYFIELD 'Navier_Stokes', a legal value this problem type cannot honour: it aborts from src/scatra/4C_scatra_dyn.cpp with 'If you want non-matching fluid and scatra meshes, you need to use FIELDCOUPLING volmortar!' — note the complaint is about meshes, not about the key — so the silence in the omitted arm is a measurement and not an unchecked path. Both diagnostics an earlier version of this entry quoted for the omission are absent (CLAIMED_VELOCITY_FIELD_NOT_FOUND=0, CLAIMED_VELNP_UNINITIALIZED=0). Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: If you want non-matching fluid and scatra meshes, you need to use FIELDCOUPLING volmortar!

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: put VELOCITYFIELD back into the omitted arm. There is then no omission under test, OMITTED_DECK_HAS_VELOCITYFIELD becomes 1 and the fixture must go red.

remove the control: run the Navier_Stokes arm with the default value. EXIT_NAVSTOKES goes to 0 and the mesh-coupling abort disappears, so the fixture must go red — that arm is the only thing showing 4C would speak up if there were anything to say.
